name: Prone leg raise
movement: one straight leg lifted a little off the floor and lowered

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to where you will be.

words.hint: Lying face down, one straight leg lifted a little off the floor.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. Lie face down side on to it, legs straight, forehead on your hands.
words.position: Lie face down, side on to the phone, legs straight, forehead resting on your hands, hips pressed into the floor.
words.top: One straight leg lifted a little off the floor — up to about ten degrees at the hip, a hand's width at the foot — hips and chest still on the floor, held.
howto: Lie face down with your forehead on your hands and both legs straight.
Tighten the buttock and lift one straight leg a little off the floor — about a hand's width at the foot. Both hip bones stay on the floor.
Hold for three seconds without lifting the hip, the chest or arching the lower back.
Lower slowly. The rep counts when the foot is back down.
words.cannot: The pelvis rolling toward the camera and the lower back muscles taking over: it sees the lift, the knee, the hip rising and the chest lifting. Lift from the buttock, not the back.
words.about: Prone leg raise — lying face down side on: the lift, as the angle at the hip between shoulder and knee read as the change from rest — the coach follows the rest slowly while the leg is near it, so one person's 172 at rest and another's 180 both count as 0; a rep is under way past 2° of lift and counts when the leg is back at rest; at the top a lift of 3–12° (about 5–15 cm at the foot; past that the lower back arches); the knee at least 155° so the leg stays straight; the hip not lifting more than 4° and the chest not more than 5° from where they started, judged through the rep. Hold three seconds at the top, lower slowly. Feet to shoulders must be in the picture; the leg measured is the one whose hip opens.
words.lost: Lie face down side on to the camera, feet to shoulders in the picture
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: This is a small lift. Stop if the lower back pinches; lift less high next time.
words.easier: A smaller lift; a pillow under the hips.
words.harder: A longer hold; an ankle weight.
words.mistakes: Lifting the hip off the floor to get height; arching the back and lifting the chest; bending the knee; lifting too high; swinging the leg out to the side.

measurements.label: lift from rest

settings.label: Lift at the top, at most (degrees from rest, negative)
Lift at the top, at least (degrees from rest, negative)

measurements.why: The angle at the hip between the shoulder and the knee, as the change from rest: lifting the leg opens it, read here as a drop below 0. A lift of 3 to 12 degrees — about 5 to 15 cm at the foot — is the exercise; past that the lower back arches. The knee, not the ankle, so a bending knee does not read as a lift.

measurements.label: working leg
measurements.why: Not judged: it picks the working leg — the one whose hip opens as the knee rises off the floor line — even by the few degrees of this lift.

measurements.label: knee straight

settings.label: Knee angle, at least (180 is straight)

measurements.why: The knee kept straight: 180 is locked out, though lying face down the model reads a straight knee at 160-168. Below the band it is bending.

measurements.label: hip above the shoulder

settings.label: Chest lifted, at most (degrees from the start, negative)
Hip lifted, at most (degrees from the start)

measurements.why: The line from the shoulder to the hip, as its change since the start: + the hip lifting off the floor (the pelvis rolling to give height), − the chest lifting (the back arching).

prompt.text: Lift one leg — just a little

faults.label: Hip lifting

faults.deep: Keep both hips flat on the floor — the hip is coming up

faults.label: Chest lifting
faults.text: Chest down — forehead on your hands

faults.label: Too high
faults.text: Not so high — a hand's width at the foot
faults.deep: Lower it — a small lift, hips on the floor

faults.label: Lift short
faults.text: Lift a little higher — a hand's width at the foot
faults.deep: Higher — a hand's width off the floor
